web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: Financial Forensics — Margin Bridges, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet Reset
question: Do the multi-year financial statements confirm genuine earnings quality, cash conversion, and capital efficiency—or do capex, working capital, and re-leveraging hide structural fragilities?

epigraph.quote: We continue to expect a stronger second half, supported by the progression of our development and commercial pipeline and the ramp-up of new capacity.
epigraph.author: Sivaramakrishnan Chittor, CFO, Sai Life Sciences

web_blocks.title: Multi-Year P&L Trajectory: Compounding Through the SaiNxt Trough (FY19–TTM Sep 2026)

web_blocks.html: From FY19 to FY26, Sai Life grew sales from ₹695 Cr to ₹2,192 Cr (17.8% 7-year CAGR) and ₹2,371 Cr on a TTM Sep 2026 basis [1]. As Chapter 1 showed, the P&L moved through two phases. First came the buildout drag (FY19–FY23), when OPM fell from 25% to 14% and PAT dropped to ₹6–₹10 Cr [1]. Then came operating leverage (FY24–TTM Sep 2026), lifting OPM back to 29% and TTM PAT to ₹376 Cr [1].

web_blocks.caption: SAILIFE Consolidated Profit & Loss Ledger (FY19–TTM Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue more than tripled from ₹695 Cr (FY19) to ₹2,371 Cr (TTM) [1]. Operating margin also doubled from its FY23 trough of 14% to 29% [1].

web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet Forensics: Short-Term Borrowing Mismatch, Leases & Credit Upgrade

web_blocks.html: The September 30, 2026 balance sheet exposes a financing risk hidden inside headline debt [1, 29]. Total Equity climbed to ₹2,688 Cr (₹21.24 Cr share capital plus ₹2,666.8 Cr reserves) [29]. Post-IPO paydowns cut debt from ₹928 Cr (Mar 2024) to ₹288 Cr (Mar 2026) [1]. During H1 FY27, however, CWIP more than doubled from ₹270.45 Cr to ₹559.60 Cr—24.3% of combined PPE and CWIP earning zero revenue today [29]. Total borrowings jumped back to ₹619.57 Cr (~₹620 Cr) [29]. Breaking down that ₹619.57 Cr reveals a sharp asset-liability maturity mismatch. Lease liabilities account for ₹171.33 Cr (₹114.76 Cr non-current, ₹56.57 Cr current), while ex-lease financial debt jumped from ₹95.13 Cr to ₹448.24 Cr [29]. Crucially, ₹417.94 Cr (93.2% of financial debt) is short-term debt due within 12 months funding multi-year plants [29]. Cash and liquid investments fell from ₹157.86 Cr to ₹107.96 Cr, swinging net financial debt from ₹62.74 Cr net cash to ₹340.28 Cr net debt [29]. On November 13, 2026, India Ratings upgraded bank loans to IND AA/Stable (short-term IND A1+) [28]. On November 24, 2026, it rated ₹100 Cr of new Axis and Kotak term loans (total rated facilities ₹869 Cr) to start terming out this bridge [27]. At the same time, India Ratings set a clear negative rating trigger at 1.5x adjusted net debt/EBITDA [27, 28].

web_blocks.caption: SAILIFE Consolidated Balance Sheet Ledger (Mar 2019–Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: September 2026 debt of ₹620 Cr includes ₹171 Cr leases, ₹30 Cr long-term loans, and ₹418 Cr short-term debt (up 5.6x in six months) bridging ₹560 Cr CWIP [1, 29]. On November 24, ₹100 Cr of new IND AA/Stable term loans began terming out that bridge [27].

web_blocks.title: Cash Flow Conversion, Unbilled Contract Assets & H1 FY27 Working Capital Drag

web_blocks.html: On an annual view, cash conversion looked strong: CFO/EBITDA hit 96% in FY24, 82% in FY25, and 86% in FY26 (₹509 Cr CFO vs. ₹349 Cr PAT) [1, 27]. H1 FY27 unaudited cash flows tell a sharper near-term story [29]. Pre-working-capital operating cash flow reached ₹345.61 Cr, but working capital absorbed ₹131.46 Cr [29]. Inventories drove a ₹91.08 Cr build (+60.3% in six months to ₹242.05 Cr), while Other Current Assets grew ₹60.79 Cr to ₹684.90 Cr [29]. That dragged H1 FY27 CFO down to ₹190.13 Cr, or 56.9% of H1 EBITDA (₹334.4 Cr) [27, 29]. Against ₹561.29 Cr of cash capex, H1 Free Cash Flow plunged to -₹371.16 Cr—extending six negative FCF years out of eight through FY26's -₹83 Cr [1, 29]. Footnotes also flag ₹511.1 Cr of FY26 unbilled contract assets (+29.0% YoY from ₹396.3 Cr), equal to 23.3% of sales under Ind AS completion accounting [27]. Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP issued a clean H1 FY27 review (relying on other auditors for two units at 5.8% of Q2 sales) [29]. Still, unbilled contract assets need tight credit checks after FY25's ₹34 Cr bad-debt provision (₹16 Cr reversed in FY26) [29].

web_blocks.caption: SAILIFE Consolidated Cash Flow Ledger (FY19–FY26, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: FY26 operating cash conversion was strong at 86% of EBITDA (₹509 Cr CFO) [1]. In H1 FY27, inventory and unbilled-asset builds pulled CFO down to 56.9% (₹190 Cr) and FCF to -₹371 Cr against ₹561 Cr cash capex [29].

web_blocks.title: Capital Efficiency (ROCE/ROE), Working Capital & Forensic Red-Flag Check

web_blocks.html: Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) jumped from 3% (FY22) and 6% (FY23) to 14% (FY25) and 20% in FY26 (19.6% Screener; 18.2% Ind-Ra) [1, 27]. ROE reached 15.4% (3-year average 12.7%) [1]. Yet India Ratings warns that heavy FY27 capex and rising CWIP will keep returns subdued until new reactors ramp [27, 28]. Working Capital Days rose from 12 in FY24 to 70 in FY26 on 97 inventory days and lower payables (182 days vs. 253), even as Debtor Days improved to 62 [1]. Tax rates stay clean near 25.1% with zero dividend payout, while FY26 took a one-time ₹8.0 Cr charge for India's new Labour Codes [1, 29]. Governance checks are solid: Deloitte's review is clean and CRISIL verified 100% IPO proceeds use [29]. Still, ESOP grants (7.47 lakh shares in FY27 YTD through Nov 5, 2026) steadily add shares, and profit-linked CEO pay doubled to ₹13.08 Cr in FY26 [29]. Most importantly, CFO Siva Chittor kept future equity raises open alongside debt if multi-year capex requires it [30].

web_blocks.caption: SAILIFE Working Capital & Return Ratios (FY19–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: ROCE expanded from 3% in FY22 to 20% in FY26, while Working Capital Days rose to 70 [1]. India Ratings expects returns to moderate over the medium term while ₹560 Cr of CWIP ramps [27].

web_blocks.title: Key Forensic Watchpoints for FY27–FY28
paragraphs: 1. Short-Term Debt Funding Long-Term Plants & 1.5x Leverage Ceiling: 93.2% of Sep 2026 financial borrowings (₹417.94 Cr of ₹448.24 Cr ex-lease debt) matures within 12 months while funding ₹1,100–₹1,300 Cr of FY27 capex (-₹371 Cr H1 FCF). Watch term-out execution beyond Nov 2026's ₹100 Cr rated term loans and Ind-Ra's 1.5x adjusted net leverage downgrade trigger [27, 29].

2. Unbilled Contract Assets (₹511 Cr) & Inventory Surge (+60% H1): Completion-basis revenue recognition left ₹511.1 Cr in unbilled contract assets at FY26 (23.3% of sales) and lifted Other Current Assets to ₹684.9 Cr alongside ₹242.1 Cr of inventories at Sep 2026—pulling H1 CFO/EBITDA to 56.9%. Any push past 90 Working Capital Days would impair ROCE [1, 27, 29].

3. Open-Ended Multi-Year Capex & Equity-Raise Optionality: Management declined 3–4 year capex guidance and stated it will take debt or return to the equity market rather than starve capex—introducing potential dilution or sustained negative FCF beyond FY27 [30].

book_paragraphs: Numbers never lie if you read all three financial statements—and the balance sheet footnotes—together. Start with the profit and loss statement from FY19 through trailing twelve months September 2026. Top-line revenue more than tripled from ₹695 crore to ₹2,371 crore, and operating profit climbed from ₹176 crore (after dipping to ₹126 crore in FY22) to ₹699 crore on a trailing basis. That is genuine operational compounding.

Now flip to the September 2026 balance sheet, because our forensic audit uncovered a financing mismatch that headline tables hide. After the December 2024 IPO slashed borrowings from ₹928 crore to ₹288 crore, total debt climbed back to ₹620 crore by September 2026 as Capital Work-in-Progress more than doubled to ₹560 crore (nearly a quarter of total plant plus CWIP earning zero current return). Break that ₹620 crore apart: ₹171 crore is Ind AS 116 lease liabilities, leaving ₹448 crore of financial borrowings—and an eye-opening ₹418 crore (93.2% of financial debt, and 97.2% of H1 FY27's borrowing surge) is short-term debt due within twelve months, funding multi-year reactors. Net financial debt swung from ₹63 crore net cash in March 2026 to ₹340 crore net debt by September 2026. India Ratings upgraded Sai Life to IND AA/Stable in November 2026 and rated ₹100 crore of new bank term loans on November 24 to begin terming out that bridge, while drawing a clear red line: sustained adjusted net leverage above 1.5x triggers a downgrade.

Next, scrutinize the cash flow statement and current assets. On a full-year basis, Sai Life passed with flying colors—generating ₹509 crore of operating cash flow in FY26 (86% CFO-to-EBITDA conversion) and tightening debtor days to 62. Yet H1 FY27 cash flows flashed a yellow light: a ₹131 crore working-capital absorption (as inventories jumped 60% in six months to ₹242 crore and other current assets climbed to ₹685 crore) pulled first-half CFO down to ₹190 crore (57% of EBITDA), producing -₹371 crore of free cash flow against ₹561 crore of cash capex. Equally important, India Ratings disclosed ₹511 crore of unbilled contract assets at FY26—23% of annual sales—reflecting Ind AS completion-basis revenue recognition ahead of customer billing.

Finally, check capital efficiency and dilution risk. ROCE climbed from 3% in FY22 to nearly 20% in FY26, yet India Ratings explicitly expects return ratios to moderate over the medium term as ₹1,100 to ₹1,300 crore of FY27 capex enters the denominator before ramping. Add recurring ESOP share allotments and CFO Siva Chittor's candid November 2026 warning that management could take more debt or return to the equity market to fund future capex, and you see why balance-sheet discipline is the single biggest forensic watchpoint for FY27 and FY28.

book_subsections.title: The Forensic Verdict on Earnings Quality & Unbilled Assets
paragraphs: Are Sai Life's earnings real? Broadly yes: 86% full-year FY26 CFO-to-EBITDA conversion, clean 25.1% corporate tax rates, Deloitte's unmodified H1 FY27 limited review, and 62-day receivable collections confirm genuine commercial demand. Yet ₹511 crore of unbilled contract assets (23.3% of FY26 sales) under Ind AS completion accounting means analysts must track contract-asset conversion into billed cash every half-year—not just reported EBITDA.

Is the business self-funding its current growth wave? Definitely not. Because FY27 capex of ₹1,100 to ₹1,300 crore is roughly double trailing operating cash flow—and H1 FY27 CFO came in at just ₹190 crore—short-term debt jumped 5.6x in six months, making timely term-loan conversion and Bidar commercial ramp-up essential to protect credit quality and ROCE.

book_subsections.title: Dilution, Governance & Capital Structure Discipline
paragraphs: Equity capital rose from ₹18 crore to ₹21.18 crore via the December 2024 IPO, and edged further to ₹21.26 crore by November 2026 via recurring ESOP exercises (7.47 lakh shares allotted in FY27 YTD). CRISIL's final monitoring report confirmed 100% of IPO proceeds went as disclosed, and total debt-to-equity remains a manageable 0.23x (net financial debt-to-equity 0.13x) as of September 2026. Still, CEO compensation more than doubled to ₹13.08 crore in FY26 on profit-linked payouts, and CFO Siva Chittor explicitly kept future equity issuance on the table alongside debt if Choutuppal capex exceeds internal cash generation.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing the Balance Sheet Through the Capex Cycle
paragraphs: Let us run a quick stress test on Sai Life's balance sheet during this ₹1,100 to ₹1,300 crore FY27 investment sprint. With trailing twelve-month EBITDA near ₹700 crore and normalized operating cash conversion around 75% to 85%, full-year internal accruals can fund roughly ₹500 to ₹600 crore of capex—leaving a ₹500 to ₹700 crore funding gap in FY27 (already evident in H1 FY27's -₹371 crore free cash flow).

Against ₹2,688 crore of net worth, ₹620 crore of consolidated debt (including ₹171 crore of leases) translates to 0.23x debt-to-equity and less than 1.0x trailing EBITDA—earning an IND AA/Stable credit rating in November 2026. The real vulnerability is maturity structure and working-capital drift: replacing ₹418 crore of short-term borrowings with long-term term loans (initiated via November 24's ₹100 crore Axis/Kotak facilities) while keeping Working Capital Days below 85–90 days and adjusted net leverage well under India Ratings' 1.5x trigger is mandatory.

book_subsections.title: Reading Return on Capital Employed Across Investment Waves
paragraphs: A common mistake when analyzing capital-intensive compounders is treating peak-cycle ROCE as permanent or trough-cycle ROCE as structural. In FY22, Sai Life's ROCE of 3% looked terrible only because ₹900 crore of newly built SaiNxt capacity sat underutilized. By FY26, as those exact same labs and reactors filled, ROCE surged to 19.6% (18.2% on Ind-Ra's consolidated measure).

Over the next eighteen months, as ₹1,100 to ₹1,300 crore of new FY27 capex (including ₹560 crore of CWIP already sitting idle on the September 2026 balance sheet) enters the denominator before generating full-year revenue, India Ratings explicitly expects return ratios to remain subdued. Your job as a long-term analyst is to track gross-block asset turnover and operating margin stability to confirm that incremental capital earns above 18% to 20% once ramped.

book_subsections.title: Why Operating Cash Flow Conversion Is the Ultimate Lie Detector
paragraphs: In specialty chemicals and contract manufacturing, reported net profit can look healthy on paper while cash quietly disappears into unbilled contract assets or inventory. Full-year FY26 operating cash flow of ₹509 crore (86% of EBITDA) was reassuring, yet H1 FY27's drop to ₹190 crore (57% of EBITDA) amid a 60% inventory jump and ₹685 crore of other current assets shows why interim cash-flow checks are non-negotiable.

If H2 FY27 commercial dispatches unwind that inventory and lift full-year CFO/EBITDA back above 75% to 80%, negative free cash flow reflects productive reinvestment; if unbilled contract assets and inventory keep swelling, cash quality is deteriorating.

book_subsections.title: Why Clean Tax Rates and Debtor Days Validate Earnings
paragraphs: Whenever you audit a fast-growing manufacturer, check two quiet forensic lines: effective tax rate and debtor days. Sai Life paid a clean 25.1% corporate tax rate in FY26 and H1 FY27 while tightening debtor collection to 62 days (trade receivables actually edged down from ₹374 crore in March 2026 to ₹342 crore in September 2026). Those two facts confirm that billed revenue collects cleanly—leaving unbilled contract assets and inventory conversion as the key working-capital watchpoints.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: There is a world of difference between bad negative free cash flow—where a company bleeds cash on unpaid receivables—and productive negative free cash flow, where ₹509 crore of real operating cash is reinvested into high-ROCE commercial reactors. Sai Life sits squarely in the second camp, but ₹620 crore of rising debt reminds us that capex timing still carries real execution risk.
